purpose: Associate a label, description and validation message with a control.
invariants: The host supplies a meaningful label and a participating control consumes Field metadata to establish its programmatic name.
Invalid state is associated with its message.
Field does not replace the input behavior.

host: one appropriate participating control per field
input behavior, value and form lifecycle

requirements.statement: Generate a control ID unless id is supplied; render the wrapper at controlId-field and label at controlId-label with htmlFor targeting the control ID. Provide the same metadata through the nearest Field context.

Compose a control that consumes useFieldControl or applies the equivalent ID/ARIA attributes. Field does not clone arbitrary children or automatically associate a plain input that ignores its context.

useFieldControl resolves id, aria-labelledby, required and disabled from explicit control props before context. aria-invalid takes precedence over explicit invalid, then contextual invalid; explicit false overrides inherited booleans.
Merge and deduplicate whitespace-separated contextual help/error IDs with caller aria-describedby IDs, retaining context references before caller references.

Render help for any value except undefined/null/false, including zero and empty string. Render error except undefined/null/false/empty string, including zero; present an existing error with role=alert.

Default contextual invalid and wrapper data-invalid from error presence, while an explicit invalid boolean overrides that inference. Error text is associated through describedby even if invalid is explicitly false.
Show required marker and hidden required wording when required; otherwise show Optional when optional. Required wins if both flags are supplied.

Own validation timing, native required application, server errors, disabled behavior of any nonparticipating children and submit/focus workflow. A context flag is metadata until the control applies it.

Supply a useful label and appropriate control identity; avoid multiple controls accidentally sharing the same generated control ID. A nonempty programmatic name is a host obligation, not runtime-validated by Field.
Use input group tokens for the Field wrapper and retain the nested control behavior/styles rather than replacing them with decorative markup.

limitations: Field is not a form validator or native disabled fieldset. Arbitrary children do not inherit browser control behavior from its div wrapper.
Help/error nodes can contain arbitrary React content; the host must keep messages and any supplied ID references meaningful.
